newsitem.title: UK: Watmoughs tumbles after limp H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Watmoughs tumbles after limp H1 results.

text.p: Shares in Watmoughs Holdings Plc tumbled on Tuesday after the printing group posted disappointing results and as one broker lowered profit forecasts for the year.
Henderson Crosthwaite said it had lowered pre-tax profit forecasts for 1996 to around 25 million stg from 26.5 million stg, and revised earnings per share to 25 pence from 28 pence.

"The results were a bit disappointing and I've lowered my forecasts, but it's still a very good company and if the stock continues to weaken I'd buy them," said Henderson Crothwaite's analyst Louise Barton.

Watmoughs said pretax profits slipped to 9.62 million stg from 10.07 million in the six months to June 30. The company said reorganisation and redundancy costs of 1.14 million stg were largely to blame for the 14 percent fall.

"But we knew this year wasn't going to be great after the loss of the gravure printing contract, but it made up for that with contracts that have come on stream from June and the rate of growth should accelerate from here," Barton said.
She added, however, that negative comments about the company's web capacity were a cause for concern.
